verses.zh: 行为完全、遵行耶和华律法的，这人便为有福！
verses.en: א (Alef)[NOTE:1]How blessed are those whose actions are blameless,[NOTE:2] who obey[NOTE:3] the law of the Lord.
notes: The psalmist celebrates God’s law and the guidance it provides his people. He expresses his desire to know God’s law thoroughly so that he might experience the blessings that come to those who obey it. This lengthy psalm exhibits an elaborate acrostic pattern. The psalm is divided into twenty-two sections (corresponding to the letters of the Hebrew alphabet), each of which is comprised of eight verses. Each of the verses in the first section (vv. 1-8) begins with the letter alef (א), the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet. This pattern continues throughout the psalm as each new section highlights a successive letter of the alphabet. Each verse in section two (vv. 9-16) begins with the second letter of the alphabet, each verse in section three (vv. 17-24) with the third letter, etc. This rigid pattern creates a sense of order and completeness and may have facilitated memorization.
Heb “[Oh] the happiness of those who are blameless of way.”
Heb “walk in.”

verses.zh: 遵守他的法度、一心寻求他的，这人便为有福！
verses.en: How blessed are those who observe his rulesand seek him with all their heart,

verses.zh: 这人不做非义的事，但遵行他的道。
verses.en: who, moreover, do no wrong,but follow in his footsteps.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “walk in his ways.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你曾将你的训词吩咐我们，为要我们殷勤遵守。
verses.en: You demand that your preceptsbe carefully kept.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “you, you commanded your precepts, to keep, very much.”

verses.zh: 但愿我行事坚定，得以遵守你的律例。
verses.en: If only I were predisposed[NOTE:1] to keep your statutes.
notes: Heb “if only my ways were established.”

verses.zh: 我看重你的一切命令，就不至于羞愧。
verses.en: Then I would not be ashamed,if[NOTE:1] I were focused on[NOTE:2] all your commands.
notes: Or “when.”
Heb “I gaze at.”

verses.zh: 我学了你公义的判语，就要以正直的心称谢你。
verses.en: I will give you sincere thanks[NOTE:1] when I learn your just regulations.
notes: Heb “I will give you thanks with an upright heart.”

verses.zh: 我必守你的律例；求你总不要丢弃我！
verses.en: I will keep your statutes.Do not completely abandon me.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “do not abandon me to excess.” For other uses of the phrase עַד מְאֹד (ʿad meʾod, “to excess”), see Ps 38:6, 8.

verses.zh: 少年人用甚么洁净他的行为呢？是要遵行你的话！
verses.en: ב (Bet)How can a young person[NOTE:1] maintain a pure life?[NOTE:2] By guarding it according to your instructions.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “young man.” Hebrew wisdom literature often assumes and reflects the male-oriented perspective of ancient Israelite society. The principle of the psalm is certainly applicable to all people, regardless of their gender or age. To facilitate modern application, the gender specific “young man” has been translated with the more neutral “young person.”
Heb “purify his path.”
Heb “by keeping according to your word.” Many medieval Hebrew mss as well as the LXX read the plural, “your words.”

verses.zh: 我一心寻求了你；求你不要叫我偏离你的命令。
verses.en: With all my heart I seek you.Do not allow me to stray from your commands.

verses.zh: 我将你的话藏在心里，免得我得罪你。
verses.en: In my heart I store up[NOTE:1] your words,[NOTE:2] so I might not sin against you.
notes: Or “hide.”
Heb “your word.” Some medieval Hebrew mss as well as the LXX read the plural, “your words.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你是应当称颂的！求你将你的律例教训我！
verses.en: You deserve praise,[NOTE:1] O Lord.Teach me your statutes.
notes: Heb “[are] blessed.”

verses.zh: 我用嘴唇传扬你口中的一切典章。
verses.en: With my lips I proclaimall the regulations you have revealed.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “of your mouth.”

verses.zh: 我喜悦你的法度，如同喜悦一切的财物。
verses.en: I rejoice in the lifestyle prescribed by your rules[NOTE:1] as if[NOTE:2] they were riches of all kinds.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “in the way of your rules.”
Heb “as upon,” meaning “as if” (see 2 Chr 32:19).
Heb “all wealth.” The phrase refers to all kinds of wealth and riches. See Prov 1:13; 6:31; 24:4; Ezek 27:12, 18.

verses.zh: 我要默想你的训词，看重你的道路。
verses.en: I will meditate on[NOTE:1] your preceptsand focus on[NOTE:2] your behavior.[NOTE:3]
notes: The cohortative verbal forms in this verse express the psalmist’s resolve.
Heb “gaze [at].”
Heb “ways” (referring figuratively to God’s behavior here).

verses.zh: 我要在你的律例中自乐；我不忘记你的话。
verses.en: I find delight[NOTE:1] in your statutes;I do not forget your instructions.[NOTE:2]
notes: The imperfects in this verse emphasize the attitude the psalmist maintains toward God’s law. Another option is to translate with the future tense, “I will find delight…I will not forget.”
Heb “your word.” Many medieval Hebrew mss as well as the LXX read the plural here.

verses.zh: 求你用厚恩待你的仆人，使我存活，我就遵守你的话。
verses.en: ג (Gimel)Be kind to your servant.Then I will live[NOTE:1] and keep[NOTE:2] your instructions.[NOTE:3]
notes: The prefixed verbal form is probably a cohortative indicating purpose/result after the preceding imperative.
The cohortative with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the imperative that begins the verse.
Heb “your word.” Many medieval Hebrew mss as well as several ancient versions read the plural here.

verses.zh: 求你开我的眼睛，使我看出你律法中的奇妙。
verses.en: Open[NOTE:1] my eyes so I can truly see[NOTE:2] the marvelous things in your law.
notes: Heb “uncover.” The verb form גַּל (gal) is an apocopated Piel imperative from גָּלָה (galah, see GKC 214 §75.cc).
The cohortative with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the preceding imperative.

verses.zh: 我是在地上作寄居的；求你不要向我隐瞒你的命令！
verses.en: I am a resident foreigner in this land.[NOTE:1] Do not hide your commands from me.
notes: Heb This metaphor probably derives from Lev 25:23, which uses the terms גֵּר (ger, “resident foreigner”) and תּוֹשָׁב; (toshav, “resident/temporary settler”). Lev 25:23 emphasizes that Israel would be a guest on God’s land. They were attached to the Lord’s household; they did not own the land. Cf. also Ps 39:12 and Gen 23:4.

verses.zh: 我时常切慕你的典章，甚至心碎。
verses.en: I desperately long to know[NOTE:1] your regulations at all times.
notes: Heb “my soul languishes for longing for.”

verses.zh: 受咒诅、偏离你命令的骄傲人，你已经责备他们。
verses.en: You reprimand arrogant people.Those who stray from your commands are doomed.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “accursed.” The traditional punctuation of the Hebrew text takes “accursed” with the previous line (“arrogant, accursed ones”), but it is preferable to take it with the second line as the predicate of the statement.

verses.zh: 求你除掉我所受的羞辱和藐视，因我遵守你的法度。
verses.en: Spare me[NOTE:1] shame and humiliation,for I observe your rules.
notes: Heb “roll away from upon me.” Some derive the imperatival form גַּל (gal) from גָּלָה (galah, “uncover,” as in v. 18), but here the form is from גָּלַל (galal, “roll”; see Josh 5:9, where חֶרְפָּה [kherpah, “shame; reproach”] also appears as object of the verb). Some, following the lead of a Dead Sea scroll (11QPsa), emend the form to גֹּל (gol).

verses.zh: 虽有首领坐着妄论我，你仆人却思想你的律例。
verses.en: Though rulers plot and slander me,[NOTE:1] your servant meditates on your statutes.
notes: Heb “though rulers sit, about me they talk together.” (For another example of the Niphal of דָּבַר (davar) used with a suffixed form of the preposition ב (bet), see Ezek 33:30.)

verses.zh: 你的法度是我所喜乐的，是我的谋士。
verses.en: Yes, I find delight in your rules;they give me guidance.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “men of my counsel.” That is, God’s rules are like advisers to the psalmist, for they teach him how to live in a godly manner that refutes the accusations of his enemies.

verses.zh: 我的性命几乎归于尘土；求你照你的话将我救活！
verses.en: ד (Dalet)I collapse in the dirt.[NOTE:1] Revive me with your word.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “my soul clings to the dirt.” The Hebrew term נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh, “being; soul”) with a pronominal suffix is often equivalent to a pronoun, especially in poetry (see BDB 660 s.v. נֶפֶשׁ 4.a).
Heb “according to your word.” Many medieval Hebrew mss read the plural “your words.”

verses.zh: 我述说我所行的，你应允了我；求你将你的律例教训我！
verses.en: I told you about my ways[NOTE:1] and you answered me.Teach me your statutes.
notes: Heb “my ways I proclaimed.”

verses.zh: 求你使我明白你的训词，我就思想你的奇事。
verses.en: Help me to understand what your precepts mean.[NOTE:1] Then I can meditate[NOTE:2] on your marvelous teachings.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the way of your precepts make me understand.”
The cohortative with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the preceding imperative.
Heb “your amazing things,” which refers here to the teachings of the law (see v. 18).

verses.zh: 我的心因愁苦而消化；求你照你的话使我坚立！
verses.en: I collapse[NOTE:1] from grief.Sustain me by your word.[NOTE:2]
notes: Some translate “my soul weeps,” taking the verb דָלַף (dalaf) from a root meaning “to drip; to drop” (BDB 196 s.v. דֶּלַף). On the basis of cognate evidence from Arabic and Akkadian, HALOT 223 s.v. II דלף proposes a homonymic root here, meaning “be sleepless.” Following L. C. Allen (Psalms 101-150 [WBC], 127, 135) the translation assumes that the verb is cognate with Ugaritic dlp, “to collapse; to crumple” in CTA 2 iv. 17, 26. See G. R. Driver, Canaanite Myths and Legends, 44, 144.
Heb “according to your word.” Many medieval Hebrew mss read the plural “your words.”

verses.zh: 求你使我离开奸诈的道，开恩将你的律法赐给我！
verses.en: Remove me from the path of deceit.[NOTE:1] Graciously give me[NOTE:2] your law.
notes: The “path of deceit” refers to a lifestyle characterized by deceit and disloyalty to God. It stands in contrast to the “way of faithfulness” in v. 30.
Heb “be gracious to me.” The verb is used metonymically here for “graciously giving” the law. (See Gen 33:5, where Jacob uses this verb in describing how God had graciously given him children.)

verses.zh: 我拣选了忠信的道，将你的典章摆在我面前。
verses.en: I choose the path of faithfulness;I am committed to[NOTE:1] your regulations.
notes: BDB 1000-1001 s.v. I שָׁוָה derives the verb from the first homonym listed, meaning “to agree with; to be like; to resemble.” It here means (in the Piel stem) “to be accounted suitable,” which in turn would mean by metonymy “to accept; to be committed to.” Some prefer to derive the verb from a homonym meaning “to place; to set,” but in this case an elliptical prepositional phrase must be understood, “I place your regulations [before me]” (see Ps 16:8).

verses.zh: 我持守你的法度；耶和华啊，求你不要叫我羞愧！
verses.en: I hold fast[NOTE:1] to your rules.O Lord, do not let me be ashamed.
notes: Or “cling to.”

verses.zh: 你开广我心的时候，我就往你命令的道上直奔。
verses.en: I run along the path of your commands,for you enable me to do so.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for you make wide my heart.” The “heart” is viewed here as the seat of the psalmist’s volition and understanding. The Lord gives the psalmist the desire and moral understanding that are foundational to the willing obedience depicted metaphorically in the preceding line. In Isa 60:5 the expression “your heart will be wide” means “your heart will swell with pride,” but here the nuance appears to be different.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你将你的律例指教我，我必遵守到底！
verses.en: ה (He)Teach me, O Lord, the lifestyle prescribed by your statutes[NOTE:1] so that I might observe it continually.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the way of your statutes.”

Heb “and I will keep it to the end.” The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the preceding imperative. The Hebrew term עֵקֶב (ʿeqev) is understood to mean “end” here. Another option is to take עֵקֶב as meaning “reward” here (see Ps 19:11) and to translate, “so that I might observe it and be rewarded.”

verses.zh: 求你赐我悟性，我便遵守你的律法，且要一心遵守。
verses.en: Give me understanding so that I might observe your lawand keep it with all my heart.[NOTE:1]
notes: The two prefixed verbal forms with vav (ו) conjunctive indicate purpose/result after the introductory imperative.

verses.zh: 求你叫我遵行你的命令，因为这是我所喜乐的。
verses.en: Guide me[NOTE:1] in the path of your commands,for I delight to walk in it.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “make me walk.”
Heb “for in it I delight.”

verses.zh: 求你使我的心趋向你的法度，不趋向非义之财。
verses.en: Give me a desire for your rules,[NOTE:1] rather than for wealth gained unjustly.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “turn my heart to your rules.”
Heb “and not unjust gain.”

verses.zh: 求你叫我转眼不看虚假，又叫我在你的道中生活。
verses.en: Turn my eyes away from what is worthless.[NOTE:1] Revive me with your word.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Make my eyes pass by from looking at what is worthless.”
Heb “by your word.”

verses.zh: 你向敬畏你的人所应许的话，求你向仆人坚定！
verses.en: Confirm to your servant your promise,[NOTE:1] which you made to the one who honors you.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “word.”
Heb “which [is] for your fear,” that is, the promise made to those who exhibit fear of God.

verses.zh: 求你使我所怕的羞辱远离我，因你的典章本为美。
verses.en: Take away the insults that I dread.[NOTE:1] Indeed,[NOTE:2] your regulations are good.
notes: Heb “my reproach that I fear.”
Or “for.”

verses.zh: 我羡慕你的训词；求你使我在你的公义上生活！
verses.en: Look, I long for your precepts.Revive me with your deliverance.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “righteousness.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，愿你照你的话，使你的慈爱，就是你的救恩，临到我身上，
verses.en: ו (Vav)May I experience your loyal love,[NOTE:1] O Lord,and your deliverance,[NOTE:2] as you promised.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and may your loyal love come to me.”
Or “salvation” (so many English versions).
Heb “according to your word.”

verses.zh: 我就有话回答那羞辱我的，因我倚靠你的话。
verses.en: Then I will have a reply for the one who insults me,[NOTE:1] for I trust in your word.
notes: Heb “and I will answer [the] one who insults me a word.” The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the jussive (see v. 41).

verses.zh: 求你叫真理的话总不离开我口，因我仰望你的典章。
verses.en: Do not completely deprive me of a truthful testimony,[NOTE:1] for I await your justice.
notes: Heb “do not snatch from my mouth a word of truth to excess.” The psalmist wants to be able to give a reliable testimony about the Lord’s loyal love (vv. 41-42), but if God does not intervene, the psalmist will be deprived of doing so, for the evidence of such love (i.e., deliverance) will be lacking.

verses.zh: 我要常守你的律法，直到永永远远。
verses.en: Then I will keep[NOTE:1] your law continuallynow and for all time.[NOTE:2]
notes: The cohortative verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the negated jussive (see v. 43).
Or “forever and ever.”

verses.zh: 我要自由而行（或译：我要行在宽阔之地），因我素来考究你的训词。
verses.en: I will be secure,[NOTE:1] for I seek your precepts.
notes: Heb “and I will walk about in a wide place.” The cohortative with prefixed vav (ו) conjunctive gives a further consequence of the anticipated positive divine response (see vv. 43-44). Another option is to take the cohortative as expressing the psalmist’s request. In this case one could translate, “and please give me security.”

verses.zh: 我也要在君王面前论说你的法度，并不至于羞愧。
verses.en: I will speak[NOTE:1] about your regulations before kingsand not be ashamed.
notes: The series of four cohortatives with prefixed vav (ו) conjunctive in vv. 46-48 list further consequences of the anticipated positive divine response to the request made in v. 43.

verses.zh: 我要在你的命令中自乐；这命令素来是我所爱的。
verses.en: I will find delight in your commands,which I love.

verses.zh: 我又要遵行（原文是举手）你的命令，这命令素来是我所爱的；我也要思想你的律例。
verses.en: I will lift my hands to[NOTE:1] your commands,which I love,and I will meditate on your statutes.
notes: Lifting the hands is often associated with prayer (Pss 28:2; 63:4; Lam 2:19). (1) Because praying to God’s law borders on the extreme, some prefer to emend the text to “I lift up my hands to you,” eliminating “your commands, which I love” as dittographic. In this view these words were accidentally repeated from the previous verse. (2) However, it is possible that the psalmist closely associates the law with God himself because he views the law as the expression of the divine will. (3) Another option is that “lifting the hands” does not refer to prayer here, but to the psalmist’s desire to receive and appropriate the law. (4) Still others understand this to be an action praising God’s commands (so NCV; cf. TEV, CEV, NLT).

verses.zh: 求你记念向你仆人所应许的话，叫我有盼望。
verses.en: ז (Zayin)Remember your word to your servant,for you have given me hope.

verses.zh: 这话将我救活了；我在患难中，因此得安慰。
verses.en: This[NOTE:1] is what comforts me in my trouble,for your promise revives me.[NOTE:2]
notes: The demonstrative “this” refers back to the hope just mentioned or forward to the statement in the second line concerning the promise’s power to revive. See the note on the word “me” at the end of the verse for further discussion.

The hope generated by the promise (see v. 49b) brings comfort because (note “for” at the beginning of the line) the promise revives the psalmist’s spirits. Another option is to take כִּי (ki) at the beginning of the second line in the sense of “that,” in which case “this” refers to the promise’s power to revive.

verses.zh: 骄傲的人甚侮慢我，我却未曾偏离你的律法。
verses.en: Arrogant people do nothing but scoff at me.[NOTE:1] Yet I do not turn aside from your law.
notes: Heb “scoff at me to excess.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，我记念你从古以来的典章，就得了安慰。
verses.en: I remember your ancient regulations,[NOTE:1] O Lord, and console myself.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I remember your regulations from of old.” The prepositional phrase “from of old” apparently modifies “your regulations,” alluding to the fact that God revealed them to Israel in the distant past. Another option is to understand the prepositional phrase as modifying the verb, in which case one might translate, “I have long remembered your regulations.”
Or “find comfort.”

verses.zh: 我见恶人离弃你的律法，就怒气发作，犹如火烧。
verses.en: Rage takes hold of me because of the wicked,those who reject your law.

verses.zh: 我在世寄居，素来以你的律例为诗歌。
verses.en: Your statutes have been my songs[NOTE:1] in the house where I live.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “songs were your statutes to me.”

Heb “in the house of my dwelling place.” Some take the Hebrew noun מָגוֹר (magor) in the sense of “temporary abode,” and see this as a reference to the psalmist’s status as a resident foreigner (see v. 19). But the noun can refer to a dwelling place in general (see Ps 55:15).

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，我夜间记念你的名，遵守你的律法。
verses.en: I remember your name during the night, O Lord,and I will keep[NOTE:1] your law.
notes: The cohortative verbal form expresses the psalmist’s resolve to obey the law.

verses.zh: 我所以如此，是因我守你的训词。
verses.en: This[NOTE:1] has been my practice,for I observe your precepts.
notes: Heb “this has been to me.” The demonstrative “this” (1) refers back to the practices mentioned in vv. 54-55, or (2) looks forward to the statement in the second line, in which case the כִּי (ki) at the beginning of the second line should be translated “that.”

verses.zh: 耶和华是我的福分；我曾说，我要遵守你的言语。
verses.en: ח (Khet)The Lord is my source of security.[NOTE:1] I have determined[NOTE:2] to follow your instructions.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “my portion [is] the Lord.” The psalmist compares the Lord to landed property, which was foundational to economic stability in ancient Israel (see Ps 16:5).
Heb “I said.”
Heb “to keep your words” (see v. 9).

verses.zh: 我一心求过你的恩；愿你照你的话怜悯我！
verses.en: I seek your favor[NOTE:1] with all my heart.Have mercy on me as you promised.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I appease your face.”
Heb “according to your word.”

verses.zh: 我思想我所行的道，就转步归向你的法度。
verses.en: I consider my actions[NOTE:1] and follow[NOTE:2] your rules.
notes: Heb “my ways.”
Heb “and I turn my feet toward.”

verses.zh: 我急忙遵守你的命令，并不迟延。
verses.en: I keep your commands eagerlyand without delay.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “I hurry and I do not delay to keep your commands.”

verses.zh: 恶人的绳索缠绕我，我却没有忘记你的律法。
verses.en: The ropes of the wicked tighten around[NOTE:1] me,but I do not forget your law.
notes: Heb “surround.”

verses.zh: 我因你公义的典章，半夜必起来称谢你。
verses.en: In the middle of the night I arise[NOTE:1] to thank youfor your just regulations.
notes: The psalmist uses an imperfect verbal form to emphasize that this is his continuing practice.

verses.zh: 凡敬畏你、守你训词的人，我都与他作伴。
verses.en: I am a friend to all your loyal followers[NOTE:1] and to those who keep your precepts.
notes: Heb “to all who fear you.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你的慈爱遍满大地；求你将你的律例教训我！
verses.en: O Lord, your loyal love fills the earth.Teach me your statutes!

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你向来是照你的话善待仆人。
verses.en: ט (Tet)You are good[NOTE:1] to your servant,O Lord, just as you promised.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “do good.”
Heb “according to your word.”

verses.zh: 求你将精明和知识赐给我，因我信了你的命令。
verses.en: Teach me proper discernment[NOTE:1] and understanding.For I consider your commands to be reliable.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “goodness of taste.” Here “taste” refers to moral and ethical discernment.
Heb “for I believe in your commands.”

verses.zh: 我未受苦以先走迷了路，现在却遵守你的话。
verses.en: Before I was afflicted I used to stray off,[NOTE:1] but now I keep your instructions.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “before I suffered, I was straying off.”
Heb “your word.”

verses.zh: 你本为善，所行的也善；求你将你的律例教训我！
verses.en: You are good and you do good.Teach me your statutes.

verses.zh: 骄傲人编造谎言攻击我，我却要一心守你的训词。
verses.en: Arrogant people smear my reputation with lies,[NOTE:1] but I observe your precepts with all my heart.
notes: Heb “smear over me a lie.”

verses.zh: 他们心蒙脂油，我却喜爱你的律法。
verses.en: Their hearts are calloused,[NOTE:1] but I find delight in your law.
notes: Heb “their heart is insensitive like fat.”

verses.zh: 我受苦是与我有益，为要使我学习你的律例。
verses.en: It was good for me to sufferso that I might learn your statutes.

verses.zh: 你口中的训言（或译：律法）与我有益，胜于千万的金银。
verses.en: The law you have revealed is more important to methan thousands of pieces of gold and silver.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “better to me [is] the law of your mouth than thousands of gold and silver.”

verses.zh: 你的手制造我，建立我；求你赐我悟性，可以学习你的命令！
verses.en: י (Yod)Your hands made me and formed me.[NOTE:1] Give me understanding so that I might learn[NOTE:2] your commands.
notes: Heb “made me and established me.” The two verbs also appear together in Deut 32:6, where God, compared to a father, is said to have “made and established” Israel.
The cohortative verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the preceding imperative.

verses.zh: 敬畏你的人见我就要欢喜，因我仰望你的话。
verses.en: Your loyal followers will be glad when they see me,[NOTE:1] for I find hope in your word.
notes: Heb “those who fear you will see me and rejoice.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，我知道你的判语是公义的；你使我受苦是以诚实待我。
verses.en: I know, Lord, that your regulations[NOTE:1] are just.You disciplined me because of your faithful devotion to me.[NOTE:2]
notes: In this context (note the second line) the Hebrew term מִשְׁפָּטִים (mishpatim), which so often refers to the regulations of God’s law elsewhere in this psalm, may refer instead to his decisions or disciplinary judgment.
Heb “and [in] faithfulness you afflicted me.”

verses.zh: 求你照着应许仆人的话，以慈爱安慰我。
verses.en: May your loyal love console me,as you promised your servant.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “according to your word to your servant.”

verses.zh: 愿你的慈悲临到我，使我存活，因你的律法是我所喜爱的。
verses.en: May I experience your compassion[NOTE:1] so I might live.For I find delight in your law.
notes: Heb “and may your compassion come to me.”

verses.zh: 愿骄傲人蒙羞，因为他们无理地倾覆我；但我要思想你的训词。
verses.en: May the arrogant be humiliated, for they have slandered me.[NOTE:1] But I meditate on your precepts.
notes: Heb “for [with] falsehood they have denied me justice.”

verses.zh: 愿敬畏你的人归向我，他们就知道你的法度。
verses.en: May your loyal followers[NOTE:1] turn to me,those who know your rules.
notes: Heb “those who fear you.”

verses.zh: 愿我的心在你的律例上完全，使我不致蒙羞。
verses.en: May I be fully committed to your statutes,[NOTE:1] so that I might not be ashamed.
notes: Heb “may my heart be complete in your statutes.”

verses.zh: 我心渴想你的救恩，仰望你的应许。
verses.en: כ (Kaf)I desperately long for[NOTE:1] your deliverance.I find hope in your word.
notes: Heb “my soul pines for.” See Ps 84:2.

verses.zh: 我因盼望你的应许眼睛失明，说：你何时安慰我？
verses.en: My eyes grow tired as I wait for your promise to be fulfilled.[NOTE:1] I say,[NOTE:2] “When will you comfort me?”
notes: Heb “my eyes fail for your word.” The psalmist has intently kept his eyes open, looking for God to intervene, but now his eyes are watery and bloodshot, impairing his vision. See Ps 69:3.
Heb “saying.”

verses.zh: 我好像烟薰的皮袋，却不忘记你的律例。
verses.en: For[NOTE:1] I am like a wineskin[NOTE:2] dried up in smoke.[NOTE:3] I do not forget your statutes.
notes: Or “even though.”
The Hebrew word נֹאד (noʾd, “leather container”) refers to a container made from animal skin which is used to hold wine or milk (see Josh 9:4, 13; Judg 4:19; 1 Sam 16:20).
Heb “in the smoke.”

verses.zh: 你仆人的年日有多少呢？你几时向逼迫我的人施行审判呢？
verses.en: How long must your servant endure this?[NOTE:1] When will you judge those who pursue me?
notes: Heb “How long are the days of your servant?”

verses.zh: 不从你律法的骄傲人为我掘了坑。
verses.en: The arrogant dig pits to trap me,[NOTE:1] which violates your law.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for me.”
Heb “which [is] not according to your law.”

verses.zh: 你的命令尽都诚实；他们无理地逼迫我，求你帮助我！
verses.en: All your commands are reliable.I am pursued without reason.[NOTE:1] Help me!
notes: God’s commands are a reliable guide to right and wrong. By keeping them the psalmist is doing what is right, yet he is still persecuted.

verses.zh: 他们几乎把我从世上灭绝，但我没有离弃你的训词。
verses.en: They have almost destroyed me here on the earth,but I do not reject your precepts.

verses.zh: 求你照你的慈爱将我救活，我就遵守你口中的法度。
verses.en: Revive me with[NOTE:1] your loyal lovethat I might keep[NOTE:2] the rules you have revealed.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “according to.”
The cohortative verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the preceding imperative.
Heb “of your mouth.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你的话安定在天，直到永远。
verses.en: ל (Lamed)O Lord, your instructions endure;they stand secure in heaven.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Forever, O Lord, your word stands firm in heaven,” or “Forever, O Lord, [is] your word; it stands firm in heaven.” The translation assumes that “your word” refers here to the body of divine instructions contained in the law (note the frequent references to the law in vv. 92-96). See vv. 9, 16-17, 57, 101, 105, 130, 139 and 160-61. The reference in v. 86 to God’s law being faithful favors this interpretation. Another option is that “your word” refers to God’s assuring word of promise, mentioned in vv. 25, 28, 42, 65, 74, 81, 107, 114, 147 and 169. In this case one might translate, “O Lord, your promise is reliable, it stands firm in heaven.”

verses.zh: 你的诚实存到万代；你坚定了地，地就长存。
verses.en: You demonstrate your faithfulness to all generations.[NOTE:1] You established the earth and it stood firm.
notes: Heb “to a generation and a generation [is] your faithfulness.”

verses.zh: 天地照你的安排存到今日；万物都是你的仆役。
verses.en: Today they stand firm by your decrees,for all things are your servants.

verses.zh: 我若不是喜爱你的律法，早就在苦难中灭绝了！
verses.en: If I had not found encouragement in your law,[NOTE:1] I would have died in my sorrow.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “if your law had not been my delight.”
Or “my suffering.”

verses.zh: 我永不忘记你的训词，因你用这训词将我救活了。
verses.en: I will never forget your precepts,for by them you have revived me.

verses.zh: 我是属你的，求你救我，因我寻求了你的训词。
verses.en: I belong to you. Deliver me!For I seek your precepts.

verses.zh: 恶人等待我，要灭绝我，我却要揣摩你的法度。
verses.en: The wicked prepare to kill me,[NOTE:1] yet I concentrate on your rules.
notes: Heb “the wicked wait for me to kill me.”

verses.zh: 我看万事尽都有限，惟有你的命令极其宽广。
verses.en: I realize that everything has its limits,but your commands are beyond full comprehension.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “to every perfection I have seen an end, your command is very wide.” God’s law is beyond full comprehension, which is why the psalmist continually studies it (vv. 95, 97).

verses.zh: 我何等爱慕你的律法，终日不住地思想。
verses.en: מ (Mem)O how I love your law!All day long I meditate on it.

verses.zh: 你的命令常存在我心里，使我比仇敌有智慧。
verses.en: Your commandments[NOTE:1] make me wiser than my enemies,for I am always aware of them.
notes: The plural form needs to be revocalized as a singular in order to agree with the preceding singular verb and the singular pronoun in the next line. The Lord’s “command” refers here to the law (see Ps 19:8).

verses.zh: 我比我的师傅更通达，因我思想你的法度。
verses.en: I have more insight than all my teachers,for I meditate on your rules.

verses.zh: 我比年老的更明白，因我守了你的训词。
verses.en: I am more discerning than those older than I,for I observe your precepts.

verses.zh: 我禁止我脚走一切的邪路，为要遵守你的话。
verses.en: I stay away[NOTE:1] from every evil path,so that I might keep your instructions.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “I hold back my feet.”
Heb “your word.” Many medieval Hebrew mss read the plural.

verses.zh: 我没有偏离你的典章，因为你教训了我。
verses.en: I do not turn aside from your regulations,for you teach me.

verses.zh: 你的言语在我上膛何等甘美，在我口中比蜜更甜！
verses.en: Your words are sweeterin my mouth than honey![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “How smooth they are to my palate, your word, more than honey to my mouth.” A few medieval Hebrew mss, as well as several other ancient witnesses, read the plural “your words,” which can then be understood as the subject of the plural verb “they are smooth.”

verses.zh: 我藉着你的训词得以明白，所以我恨一切的假道。
verses.en: Your precepts give me discernment.Therefore I hate all deceitful actions.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “every false path.”

verses.zh: 你的话是我脚前的灯，是我路上的光。
verses.en: נ (Nun)Your word[NOTE:1] is a lamp to walk byand a light to illumine my path.[NOTE:2]
notes: Many medieval Hebrew mss read the plural (“words”).
Heb “[is] a lamp for my foot and a light for my path.”

verses.zh: 你公义的典章，我曾起誓遵守，我必按誓而行。
verses.en: I have vowed and solemnly swornto keep your just regulations.

verses.zh: 我甚是受苦；耶和华啊，求你照你的话将我救活！
verses.en: I am suffering terribly.O Lord, revive me with your word.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “according to your word.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你悦纳我口中的赞美为供物，又将你的典章教训我！
verses.en: O Lord, please accept the freewill offerings of my praise.[NOTE:1] Teach me your regulations.
notes: Heb “of my mouth.”

verses.zh: 我的性命常在危险之中，我却不忘记你的律法。
verses.en: My life is in continual danger,[NOTE:1] but I do not forget your law.
notes: Heb “my life [is] in my hands continually.”

verses.zh: 恶人为我设下网罗，我却没有偏离你的训词。
verses.en: The wicked lay a trap for me,but I do not wander from your precepts.

verses.zh: 我以你的法度为永远的产业，因这是我心中所喜爱的。
verses.en: I claim your rules as my permanent possession,for they give me joy.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for the joy of my heart [are] they.”

verses.zh: 我的心专向你的律例，永远遵行，一直到底。
verses.en: I am determined to obey[NOTE:1] your statutesat all times, to the very end.
notes: Heb “I turn my heart to do.”

verses.zh: 心怀二意的人为我所恨；但你的律法为我所爱。
verses.en: ס (Samek)I hate people with divided loyalties,[NOTE:1] but I love your law.
notes: Heb “divided ones.” The word occurs only here; it appears to be derived from a verbal root, attested in Arabic, meaning “to split” (see HALOT 762 s.v. *סֵעֵף). Since the psalmist is emphasizing his unswerving allegiance to God and his law, the term probably refers to those who lack such loyalty. The translation is similar to that suggested by L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 131.

verses.zh: 你是我藏身之处，又是我的盾牌；我甚仰望你的话语。
verses.en: You are my hiding place and my shield.I find hope in your word.

verses.zh: 作恶的人哪，你们离开我吧！我好遵守我　神的命令。
verses.en: Turn away from me, you evil men,so that I can observe[NOTE:1] the commands of my God.[NOTE:2]
notes: The cohortative verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the preceding imperative.
The psalmist has already declared that he observes God’s commands despite persecution, so here the idea must be “so that I might observe the commands of my God unhindered by threats.”

verses.zh: 求你照你的话扶持我，使我存活，也不叫我因失望而害羞。
verses.en: Sustain me as you promised,[NOTE:1] so that I will live.[NOTE:2] Do not disappoint me.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “according to your word.”
The prefixed verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the preceding imperative.
Heb “do not make me ashamed of my hope.” After the Hebrew verb בּוֹשׁ (bosh, “to be ashamed”) the preposition מִן (min, “from”) often introduces the reason for shame.

verses.zh: 求你扶持我，我便得救，时常看重你的律例。
verses.en: Support me so that I will be delivered.Then I will focus[NOTE:1] on your statutes continually.
notes: Or “and that I might focus.” The two cohortatives with vav (ו) conjunctive indicate purpose/result after the imperative at the beginning of the verse.

verses.zh: 凡偏离你律例的人，你都轻弃他们，因为他们的诡诈必归虚空。
verses.en: You despise[NOTE:1] all who stray from your statutes,for such people are deceptive and unreliable.[NOTE:2]
notes: The Hebrew verb סָלָה (salah, “to disdain”) occurs only here and in Lam 1:15. Cognate usage in Aramaic and Akkadian, as well as Lam 1:15, suggest it may have a concrete nuance of “to throw away.”
Heb “for their deceit [is] falsehood.”

verses.zh: 凡地上的恶人，你除掉他，好像除掉渣滓；因此我爱你的法度。
verses.en: You remove all the wicked of the earth like slag.[NOTE:1] Therefore I love your rules.[NOTE:2]
notes: Traditionally “dross” (so KJV, ASV, NIV). The metaphor comes from metallurgy; “slag” is the substance left over after the metallic ore has been refined.
As he explains in the next verse, the psalmist’s fear of judgment motivates him to obey God’s rules.

verses.zh: 我因惧怕你，肉就发抖；我也怕你的判语。
verses.en: My body[NOTE:1] trembles[NOTE:2] because I fear you;[NOTE:3] I am afraid of your judgments.
notes: Heb “my flesh.”
The Hebrew verb סָמַר (samar, “to tremble”) occurs only here and in Job 4:15.
Heb “from fear of you.” The pronominal suffix on the noun is an objective genitive.

verses.zh: 我行过公平和公义，求你不要撇下我给欺压我的人！
verses.en: ע (Ayin)I do what is fair and right.[NOTE:1] Do not abandon me to my oppressors.
notes: Heb “do justice and righteousness.”

verses.zh: 求你为仆人作保，使我得好处，不容骄傲人欺压我！
verses.en: Guarantee the welfare of your servant.[NOTE:1] Do not let the arrogant oppress me.
notes: Heb “be surety for your servant for good.”

verses.zh: 我因盼望你的救恩和你公义的话眼睛失明。
verses.en: My eyes grow tired as I wait for your deliverance,[NOTE:1] for your reliable promise to be fulfilled.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “my eyes fail for your deliverance.” The psalmist has intently kept his eyes open, looking for God to intervene, but now his eyes are watery and bloodshot, impairing his vision. See the similar phrase in v. 82.
Heb “and for the word of your faithfulness.”

verses.zh: 求你照你的慈爱待仆人，将你的律例教训我。
verses.en: Show your servant your loyal love.[NOTE:1] Teach me your statutes.
notes: Heb “do with your servant according to your loyal love.”

verses.zh: 我是你的仆人，求你赐我悟性，使我得知你的法度。
verses.en: I am your servant. Give me insight,so that I can understand[NOTE:1] your rules.
notes: or “know.” The cohortative verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the preceding imperative.

verses.zh: 这是耶和华降罚的时候，因人废了你的律法。
verses.en: It is time for the Lord to act—they break your law.

verses.zh: 所以，我爱你的命令胜于金子，更胜于精金。
verses.en: For this reason[NOTE:1] I love your commandsmore than gold, even purest gold.
notes: “For this reason” connects logically with the statement made in v. 126. Because the judgment the psalmist fears (see vv. 119-120) is imminent, he remains loyal to God’s law.

verses.zh: 你一切的训词，在万事上我都以为正直；我却恨恶一切假道。
verses.en: For this reason I carefully follow all your precepts.[NOTE:1] I hate all deceitful actions.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “for this reason all the precepts of everything I regard as right.” The phrase “precepts of everything” is odd. It is preferable to take the כ (kaf) on כֹּל (kol, “everything) with the preceding form as a pronominal suffix, “your precepts,” and the ל (lamed) with the following verb as an emphatic particle. See L. C. Allen, Psalms 101-150 (WBC), 138.
Heb “every false path.”

verses.zh: 你的法度奇妙，所以我一心谨守。
verses.en: פ (Pe)Your rules are marvelous.Therefore I observe them.

verses.zh: 你的言语一解开就发出亮光，使愚人通达。
verses.en: Your instructions are a doorway through which light shines.[NOTE:1] They give[NOTE:2] insight to the untrained.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “the doorway of your words gives light.” God’s “words” refer here to the instructions in his law (see vv. 9, 57).
Heb “it [i.e., the doorway] gives.”
Or “the [morally] naive,” that is, the one who is young and still in the process of learning right from wrong and distinguishing wisdom from folly. See Pss 19:7; 116:6.

verses.zh: 我张口而气喘，因我切慕你的命令。
verses.en: I open my mouth and pant,because I long[NOTE:1] for your commands.
notes: The verb occurs only here in the OT.

verses.zh: 求你转向我，怜悯我，好像你素常待那些爱你名的人。
verses.en: Turn toward me and extend mercy to me,as you typically do to your loyal followers.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “according to custom toward the lovers of your name.” The “lovers of” God’s “name” are the Lord’s loyal followers. See Pss 5:11; 69:36; Isa 56:6.

verses.zh: 求你用你的话使我脚步稳当，不许甚么罪孽辖制我。
verses.en: Direct my steps by your word.[NOTE:1] Do not let any sin dominate me.
notes: God’s “word” refers here to his law (see v. 11).

verses.zh: 求你救我脱离人的欺压，我要遵守你的训词。
verses.en: Deliver me[NOTE:1] from oppressive men,so that I can keep[NOTE:2] your precepts.
notes: Or “redeem me.”
The cohortative verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the preceding imperative.

verses.zh: 求你用脸光照仆人，又将你的律例教训我。
verses.en: Smile[NOTE:1] on your servant.Teach me your statutes!
notes: Heb “cause your face to shine.”

verses.zh: 我的眼泪下流成河，因为他们不守你的律法。
verses.en: Tears stream down from my eyes,[NOTE:1] because people[NOTE:2] do not keep your law.
notes: Heb “[with] flowing streams my eyes go down.”
Heb “they”; even though somewhat generic, the referent (people) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你是公义的；你的判语也是正直的！
verses.en: צ (Tsade)You are just, O Lord,and your judgments are fair.

verses.zh: 你所命定的法度是凭公义和至诚。
verses.en: The rules you impose are just[NOTE:1] and absolutely reliable.
notes: Heb “you commanded [in] justice your rules.”

verses.zh: 我心焦急，如同火烧，因我敌人忘记你的言语。
verses.en: My zeal[NOTE:1] consumes[NOTE:2] me,for my enemies forget your instructions.[NOTE:3]
notes: or “zeal.”
Heb “destroys,” in a hyperbolic sense.
Heb “your words.”

verses.zh: 你的话极其精炼，所以你的仆人喜爱。
verses.en: Your word is absolutely pure,and your servant loves it.

verses.zh: 我微小，被人藐视，却不忘记你的训词。
verses.en: I am insignificant and despised,yet I do not forget your precepts.

verses.zh: 你的公义永远长存；你的律法尽都真实。
verses.en: Your justice endures,[NOTE:1] and your law is reliable.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “your justice [is] justice forever.”
Or “truth.”

verses.zh: 我遭遇患难愁苦，你的命令却是我所喜爱的。
verses.en: Distress and hardship confront[NOTE:1] me,yet I find delight in your commands.
notes: Heb “find.”

verses.zh: 你的法度永远是公义的；求你赐我悟性，我就活了。
verses.en: Your rules remain just.[NOTE:1] Give me insight so that I can live.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “just are your rules forever.”
The cohortative verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the preceding imperative.

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，我一心呼吁你；求你应允我，我必谨守你的律例！
verses.en: ק (Qof)I cried out with all my heart, “Answer me, O Lord!I will observe your statutes.”

verses.zh: 我向你呼吁，求你救我！我要遵守你的法度。
verses.en: I cried out to you, “Deliver me,so that I can keep[NOTE:1] your rules.”
notes: The cohortative verbal form with vav (ו) conjunctive indicates purpose/result after the preceding imperative.

verses.zh: 我趁天未亮呼求；我仰望了你的言语。
verses.en: I am up before dawn crying for help.I find hope in your word.

verses.zh: 我趁夜更未换将眼睁开，为要思想你的话语。
verses.en: My eyes anticipate the nighttime hoursso that I can meditate on your word.

verses.zh: 求你照你的慈爱听我的声音；耶和华啊，求你照你的典章将我救活！
verses.en: Listen to me[NOTE:1] because of[NOTE:2] your loyal love.O Lord, revive me, as you typically do.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “my voice.”
Heb “according to.”
Heb “according to your custom.”

verses.zh: 追求奸恶的人临近了；他们远离你的律法。
verses.en: Those who are eager to do[NOTE:1] wrong draw near;they are far from your law.
notes: Heb “those who pursue.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，你与我相近；你一切的命令尽都真实！
verses.en: You are near, O Lord,and all your commands are reliable.[NOTE:1]
notes: Or “truth.”

verses.zh: 我因学你的法度，久已知道是你永远立定的。
verses.en: I learned long ago thatyou ordained your rules to last.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “long ago I knew concerning your rules, that forever you established them.” See v. 89 for the same idea. The translation assumes that the preposition מִן (min) prefixed to “your rules” introduces the object of the verb יָדַע (yadaʿ), as in 1 Sam 23:23. Another option is that the preposition indicates source, in which case one might translate, “Long ago I realized from your rules that forever you established them” (cf. NIV, NRSV).

verses.zh: 求你看顾我的苦难，搭救我，因我不忘记你的律法。
verses.en: ר (Resh)See my pain and rescue me.For I do not forget your law.

verses.zh: 求你为我辨屈，救赎我，照你的话将我救活。
verses.en: Fight for me[NOTE:1] and defend me.[NOTE:2] Revive me with your word.
notes: Or “argue my case.”

"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Opening Statement

As one who loves the Bible and has spent his life stuyding it, this Psalm is a special treasure (as is Psalm 19). The
Bible, God's written word, has allowed me to come to know God's Living Word, Jesus (cf. John 1:1-14; Phil. 2:6-11; Col. 1:13-16;
Heb. 1:2-3). The Spirit's illumination has allowed me to do as Ezra did (Ezra 7:10, i.e., seek, practice, teach).

Psalm 119 reflects

- a blessing, Ps. 119:1

- a lifestyle faith, Ps. 119:1-2

- a lamp to my feet and a light to my path, Ps. 119:105

I commend it to you with great joy, peace, and hope that it will effectively produce

- a desire to study the Bible

- a desire to live the Bible

- a deeper personal relationship with the Triune God

One more explanation about how I approached this lengthy Psalm. It is so long and repetitive that
I decided to deal with each stanza (i.e., each consecutive letter of the Hebrew alphabet). I have tried to deal with
the uniqueness of each unit and not do an overall summary.

- Historical Setting

- The Arabic translation lists David as the author.

- Dahood, in the Anchor Bible Commentary, asserts that a united monarchal (Saul ‒ Solomon) date
is very possible. He comes to this by

- comparing this Psalm with its translation found among the Dead Sea Scrolls

- this Psalm contains many pre-exilic elements

- Leupold sees the setting as post-exilic (Ezra, Nehemiah, Haggai, Malachi). He bases this on:

- the problems related to resettlement and persecution mentioned so often in the Psalms

- the absence of any mention of the sacrificial system caused him to believe that the absence of the temple
and its ritual, along with an increase in the place of Bible study, fits an early post-exilic setting best (local
synagogues started during the Neo-Babylon exile).

- The occasion for this Psalm is joy (cf. Ps. 119:14,16,24,35,47,70,77,92,111,143,162,174) and trust in God and His
revealed truth amidst persecution. This knowledge of YHWH's character and promises brings peace and stability to troubled times.

- Literary Elements

- This, like Psalms 9-10; 25; 34; 37; 111; 112; and 145, is an acrostic based on the twenty-two letters of the Hebrew
alphabet. This same form is found in Prov. 31:10-31 and the first four chapters of Lamentations. This is the longest
and most highly developed acrostic in the Bible. Each Hebrew letter starts eight verses.

- There is a recurrent theme in every verse of this Psalm related to God's teachings to mankind. The author uses
several synonyms for the Law (cf. Ps. 19:7-9):

- the Law ‒ used 25 times

- the testimonies ‒ used 23 times

- the precepts ‒ used 21 times

- the statutes ‒ used 20 times

- the commandments ‒ used 22 times

- the judgments ‒ used 23 times

- the Word ‒ used 24 times

- the words ‒ used 19 times

- the way ‒ used 13 times

- the truth or faithfulness ‒ used 5 times

- the righteousness ‒ used 14 times

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS FOR
GOD'S REVELATION

- Kimchi's (i.e., a Jewish commentator, A.D. 1160-1235) definitions of the synonyms
used for God's revelation to man:

- the Law ‒ "it is the setting down of duties and how they are to be done"

- the testimonies ‒ "precepts that are for a testimony or federal communication"

- the precepts ‒ used "precepts which reason teaches that are, as it were, deposited in our nature"

- the statutes ‒ "precepts whose reason is not known"

- the judgments ‒ "the judgments that pass between a man and his neighbor"

- the way ‒ "the way is the rule upon which the Scripture is grounded"

- God's revelation and God's person are merged in this Psalm. To know God's revelation is to know Him. To cling
to God's revelation is to cling to Him (i.e., compare Ps. 119:31a with Deut. 10:20).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

- Be sure to notice and identify the Hebrew parallelisms. See
